chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Paul Barbarin's way with people and Steele looking after Danny
summary: Paul called everybody brother and asked Steele to look out for Danny, whom musicians called Little Barbarin.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: He and I became friends because he was a friend of... See, Paul had a way of getting to people -- my uncle.
Yeah. 'How you doin', buddy? How's everything?' A smile for everybody.
Yeah. He was a nice man.
And he'd move in on you, and said 'Hello,' and he would help you. He was good. He was good people. He went to... Nearly everybody in New York knows PB, Old Paul...

Steele(?) had him called Big Brother. Even the racketeers, like Bob Ewing and them...Blue and all of them, he said, "Hey, big brother." He'd call him and give himself protection gettin' in with them hoodlums. That's my big brother. "How you doin, big brother?" "Talkin' to Blue." Blue was one of the baddest hoodlums that ever lived. He'd say, "Hey, Blue, Mister Blue, how you doin', Blue." He'd get with everybody. Everybody. "Hello, Brother, Cousin, Bub." He'd give you a name so he would remember." Where did this man come from? Is this man(?) that I call (?) brother gonna accept me? Is he as well-dressed as me? You know, it's a psychological thing...

So everywhere Paul went... So they called me "Little Peewee" or "Little Barbarin." Most of the musicians when I first went there called "Little Barbarin." So I meet Steele(?). Paul would say, "Steele(?), look out for him, because he's just come from down there. He don't know much. He thinks he knows, you know." Steele(?) said, "I'll pull his coat." So Steele(?) would tell me everything...always... I've never forgotten. He always kept explaining me things until I left New York.
He'd see people, and he'd see... He'd tell me who they was. How much weight they carried. Who was what.
